items.title: For a dominant ring map there is a subalgebra whose spectrum map is a universal homeomorphism and which contains the images of all such factorizations
items.author: The Stacks Project Authors

items.difficulty_reason: The lemma produces, for a dominant ring map, a subalgebra whose spectrum map over the base is a universal homeomorphism and which contains the image of every factorization whose middle term has that property (statement lines 14747-14758). The counted proof, 51 lines, is a construction with two verifications: it first reduces to reduced rings by observing that a solution for the reduced map can be pulled back along the surjection onto the reduction, then defines the candidate subalgebra as the set of elements generated by finitely many generators satisfying square and cube relations or a prime multiple and a p-th power relation over the base, proves it is a subalgebra from stability of the relation pattern under concatenation of two lists of generators, and derives the two required properties from the structure result for finite type algebras inducing universal homeomorphisms (proof lines 14760-14810). It is H2 under the lane rule: both a construction and its two non-formal verifications are supplied, and no clause of the statement is left to the reader.
